    username      TEXT NOT NULL

    password_hash TEXT NOT NULL

    access_rights TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'user'

  registrations always use the salted format.

_USERNAME_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{3,50}$")
_EMAIL_RE = re.compile(r"^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$")
_MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH = 8

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
    id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    username      TEXT NOT NULL,
    email         TEXT NOT NULL,
    password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_date  TEXT NOT NULL,
    access_rights TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'user'
);

    """Open a connection and make sure the ``users`` table exists."""
    conn = sqlite3.connect(str(db_path))
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
    conn.execute(_SCHEMA)
    return conn

    """Return a salted PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 hash string for a new password."""
    salt = os.urandom(_SALT_BYTES)
    digest = hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac(
        "sha256", password.encode("utf-8"), salt, _ITERATIONS
    )
    return f"{_ALGORITHM}${_ITERATIONS}${salt.hex()}${digest.hex()}"


def verify_password(password: str, stored_hash: str) -> bool:

    Supports both the salted PBKDF2 format written for new accounts and the
    unsalted SHA-256 hex digests written by the older version of this
    database. Comparisons use ``hmac.compare_digest`` to avoid timing leaks.
